dm: If things were accomplished by one's own independent will, Then since no one desires to suffer, Suffering would never arise For any embodied being at all.
gm: If things were accomplished by their own will, Since no one desires suffering, For all embodied beings, Suffering would not occur for anyone.

dm: Through heedlessness, people even harm themselves With thorns and the like; For the sake of obtaining women and other such objects, They are consumed by craving and engage in fasting and the like.
gm: Due to carelessness, even to themselves, They do harm with thorns and so forth; In order to obtain women and the like, They become obsessed and starve themselves and so forth.

dm: Some hang themselves or leap from cliffs, Consume poison or unwholesome food, And through non-meritorious conduct, They inflict harm upon themselves.
gm: Some hang themselves or jump from cliffs, Eat poison or unwholesome food, And through non-meritorious conduct, They bring harm upon themselves.

dm: When they are under the power of afflictions, They even kill their own beloved selves; At that time, how could they possibly Refrain from harming the bodies of others?
gm: When, overpowered by afflictions, They even kill their beloved selves, At that time, to the bodies of others, How could they not cause harm?

dm: Since they are driven by the arising of afflictions To engage in such acts as killing themselves, If compassion does not arise for them, What is the point of becoming angry?
gm: When, due to the arising of afflictions, They engage in killing themselves and so forth, If compassion does not at least arise, What point is there in becoming angry?

dm: If it is the nature of the childish To cause harm to others, It is inappropriate to be angry with them; It is like resenting fire for its nature to burn.
gm: If doing harm to others Is the nature of the childish, It is illogical to become angry at them, Like resenting fire for its nature of burning.

dm: Alternatively, if this fault is adventitious And sentient beings are gentle by nature, It is still inappropriate to be angry, Just as it is to resent the sky for being filled with smoke.
gm: But if that fault is adventitious, And the nature of sentient beings is gentle, Even then it is illogical to become angry, Like resenting space when smoke arises in it.

dm: If I am angry at the one who throws it Because they directly employed a stick or other weapon, Then since they too were incited by hatred, It is more appropriate to be angry at that hatred.
gm: Although sticks and the like are directly utilized, If I become angry at the one who wields them, Since they too are impelled by hatred, It is logical to be angry at hatred.

dm: In the past, I myself inflicted Such harm upon sentient beings; Therefore, it is only right that this harm Should befall me, who caused injury to others.
gm: In the past, to sentient beings, I have done harm such as this; Therefore, since I have harmed sentient beings, It is logical that this harm comes to me.

dm: Both his weapon and my body Are the causes of this suffering. Since he has drawn the weapon and I have provided the body, At whom should I be angry?
gm: Their weapons and my body Are both causes of suffering; They produced the weapon and I the body, At which one should I be angry?

dm: This body is like a human-shaped abscess, Painful and unable to bear being touched. Since I, blinded by craving, have grasped it, At whom should I be angry when it is harmed?
gm: Like a human-shaped ulcer, Painful and unable to bear being touched; When, blinded by craving, I have grasped it, When it is harmed, at whom should I be angry?

dm: Childish beings do not desire suffering, Yet they crave the causes of suffering. Since they are harmed by their own faults, Why should they be resentful toward others?
gm: Childish ones do not desire suffering, Yet they crave the causes of suffering; When harmed by my own faults, Why should I resent others?

dm: For example, just as the guardians of hell And the forest of sword-leaves are produced By one's own karma, At whom should I be angry?
gm: Like the guardians of hell, And the forest of sword-leaves, This is produced by my own karma, So at whom should I be angry?

dm: Impelled by my own past actions, Those who harm me have arisen; If by this they go to the hells, Have I not been the one to ruin them?
gm: Instigated by my own karma, Those who harm me appear; If because of this they go to hell, Have I not ruined them?

dm: By relying on these people, My many sins are purified through patience; Yet by relying on me, They go to the hells of long-lasting suffering.
gm: By relying upon them, Through patience my many negative actions are cleansed; But by relying upon me, they Will go to the long-lasting suffering of hell.

dm: I am the one who causes them harm, And they are the ones who benefit me; Why, then, O wicked mind, Do you perversely become angry?
gm: I am the one who harms them, While they are the ones who benefit me; Why perversely, O wicked mind, do you become angry?

dm: If I possess the virtue of a patient intention, I shall not go to the hells; If I protect myself, What harm has been done to them in this?
gm: If I possess the good qualities Of intention, I will not go to hell; If I protect myself, What will happen to them here?

dm: However, if I retaliate with harm, They will not be protected, And my own conduct will also be ruined; Thus, my ascetic practice will be destroyed.
gm: But if I cause harm in return, They will not be protected, And my conduct will also decline; Thus my ascetic practice will be destroyed.

dm: Since the mind is not a physical entity, No one can destroy it anywhere; Because of intense attachment to the body, The body is afflicted by sufferings.
gm: Because the mind is bodiless, No one can destroy it anywhere; Because of deep attachment to the body, The body is harmed by sufferings.

dm: If contempt, harsh speech, And unpleasant words Do not cause any harm to the body, Why, O mind, do you become so angry?
gm: Contempt, speaking harsh words, And those unpleasant words— Since they do not harm the body, O mind, why do you become so angry?

dm: If the dislike that others have for me Does not consume me in this life or in other lives, Why should I be averse to it?
gm: That others dislike me, Since that, in this life or another, Will not consume me, Why do I dislike it?

dm: If I am averse to this because it creates obstacles to my gain, My gains will be discarded in this world, But my sins will remain firm.
gm: Because it hinders my gain, If I do not desire this, My gain will be left behind here, But my negative actions will remain steadfast.

dm: It is better that I die this very day Than to live a long life through wrong livelihood; Even if I were to remain for a long time, The suffering of death will be exactly the same.
gm: It is better that I die this very day, Than to live long by wrong livelihood; Even if I remain for a long time, The suffering of death will be just the same.

dm: Suppose one person experiences happiness for a hundred years in a dream and then wakes up, And another experiences happiness for just a brief moment and then wakes up;
gm: Having experienced happiness in a dream for a hundred years, Whoever awakens, And having experienced happiness for just an instant, Whoever awakens—

dm: For both of those who have awakened, That happiness never returns. Whether one’s life is long or short, At the time of death, it is exactly the same.
gm: For both of those who awaken, That happiness will not return; For both a long life and a short life, At the time of death they end up just the same.

dm: Even if one acquires great wealth And enjoys happiness for a long time, Just like someone plundered by thieves, One will depart naked and empty-handed.
gm: Even if I acquire abundant gains, And enjoy happiness for a long time, Just like being robbed by a thief, I will depart naked and empty-handed.

dm: If you think, "I shall live on my gains And, while doing so, exhaust my sins and perform merit," Yet you become angry for the sake of that gain, Will your merit not be exhausted and will you not incur sin?
gm: If you say, "By living on account of gains, I will exhaust negative actions and perform merit," If I become angry for the sake of gains, Will not merit be exhausted and negative actions created?

dm: If the very purpose for which I live Is itself undermined, What is the use of a life That consists only of committing sins?
gm: That very purpose for which I live, If it is destroyed, That performs only negative actions— What is the use of such a life?

dm: If you say you are angry at those who speak unpleasantly Because they harm sentient beings, Then why are you not likewise angry When others are spoken of unpleasantly?
gm: If you say, "Because it causes sentient beings to lose faith, I become angry at those who speak unpleasant words," When unpleasant words are spoken about others, Why do you not likewise become angry?

dm: Since a lack of faith depends on others, If you can tolerate those who have no faith, Then since the arising of afflictions depends on others, Why can you not tolerate those who speak unpleasantly?
gm: Because lack of faith depends on others, If you tolerate those without faith, Because it depends on the arising of afflictions, Why do you not tolerate those who speak unpleasant words?

dm: Toward those who revile and destroy Sacred images, stupas, and the sublime Dharma, It is not appropriate for me to feel hatred, For the Buddhas and the like cannot be harmed.
gm: Towards images, stupas, and the sublime Dharma, Even if someone disparages or destroys them, It is inappropriate for me to have anger, For the Buddhas and so forth suffer no harm.

dm: Toward those who cause harm to my Gurus, relatives, and friends, I should see that these events arise from conditions, As previously explained, and thus restrain my anger.
gm: Towards gurus, relatives, and so forth, And even those who do harm to friends, Through conditions, in the previous manner, Seeing that it occurs, turn back anger.

dm: Since harm is inflicted upon embodied beings By both those with minds and those without, Why single out and bear a grudge against those with minds? Therefore, you should endure all harm.
gm: To embodied beings, animate And inanimate things both do harm; Why single out the animate and hold resentment? Therefore, be patient with harm.

dm: Some commit misdeeds out of delusion; If others, being deluded, become angry, Who among them is without fault, And who is the one who is at fault?
gm: Some commit faults through ignorance, And some, being ignorant, become angry. Among them, who is to be considered faultless? And who is to be considered at fault?
